We can use the standard power-reduction identity for \(\sin^7 x\). Starting from

\[
\sin x=\frac{e^{ix}-e^{-ix}}{2i},
\]

we get

\[
\sin^7 x=\frac{i}{128}(e^{ix}-e^{-ix})^7.
\]

Expanding and pairing conjugate terms gives

\[
\sin^7 x
= -\frac{1}{64}\sin 7x+\frac{7}{64}\sin 5x-\frac{21}{64}\sin 3x+\frac{35}{64}\sin x.
\]

Thus the coefficient of \(\sin x\) is

\[
d=\frac{35}{64}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{35}{64}}
\]
